name: @guardbee/mcp-rug-pull-detector
description: MCP server that connects to another MCP server (stdio or Streamable HTTP), baselines its tools/list response, and detects 'rug pulls' — a tool silently changing description, schema, or annotations after it was already approved
long_description: Unlike guardbee-mcp's static-source scanners, this one connects live to a target MCP server (spawning it over stdio, or opening a Streamable HTTP session) and calls the real tools/list RPC. On first contact it stores a trust-on-first-use baseline (a canonical hash of each tool's name, description, input/output schema, and annotations). On every later check, it re-fetches the live tool list and flags any tool whose definition changed since baseline as critical — the documented 'MCP rug pull' pattern, where a server presents one tool definition at approval time and a different one afterward. New tools are flagged medium (could be a legitimate release, still worth review); removed tools are flagged low. No API key required — runs entirely locally, the only network/process activity is connecting to the server you point it at.
